                           ORDER ON APPEAL OF ORDER NO. 13

       This Order addresses the appeals filed by Save the Lampasas and 4K Land and Cattle
Company of Order No. 13, which denied their requests for a preliminary hearing on route
adequacy. The Commission denies the appeals ofthe administrative law judges' (ALJs') ruling in
Order No. 13 for the reasons discussed in this Order.

                                            I.   Appeals
       On May 6,2026, Save the Lampasas and 4K Land and Cattle Company filed requests for
a hearing on the adequacy of the routing alternatives available in this proceeding. Save the
Lampasas argues that the application limits the proposed routes to three corridors of links through
the northeastern portion of Burnet County.1 Save the Lampasas asserts that the routing options
available to the Commission should not be restricted to the proposed corridors in northeastern
Burnet County but should follow existing compatible corridors; therefore, Save the Lampasas
advocates for the addition of routing options.2 Save the Lampasas suggests that the applicants

should enlarge the study area and study routes north of Fort Hood that can be even further enhanced
by moving the proposed new substation associated with this project to the north.3 Alternatively,
Save the Lampasas promotes two other routes, alternate route G and route G4, within the existing
study area.4

       4K Land and Cattle Company argues that, despite the large number of filed routes, the
applicants did not provide a diverse set of choices for the Commission to consider.5 4K Land and
Cattle Company argues that the study area for the proposed transmission line is unreasonably
narrow considering the transmission line's proposed length and that there is a lack of geographic
diversity in the proposed routing alternatives. 6 4K Land and Cattle Company contends that
although 122 routes were filed, they collapse into five main corridors and that each corridor shares
many common segments with each other.7 Thus, 4K Land and Cattle Company asserts that the
122 routes are largely composed of minor variations on the same few paths.8

                                     Il.   Applicants' Response
       The applicants assert that they presented a robust number of geographically diverse routes
that were developed in consideration of the objective, observable constraints in and around the
study area.9 The applicants present five corridor options in the application in consideration ofthe
existing constraints attributed to Fort Hood, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers property, and Lake
Buchanan.'0 The applicants explain that the existing constraints in the study area prevent the
addition of routing alternatives requested by the appellants." Further, the applicants support the

size and shape of the study area, explaining that the endpoints determined by the Electric

therefore, routes that swing far north or south "would necessarily double-back, increasing mileage
and costs, and running contrary to the requirement that routing alternatives be reasonably forward
progressing. 5,12

                                            III. Discussion
        The question before the Commission is whether the ALJs properly denied the requests for
a route adequacy hearing.          The route-adequacy standard articulated in the Commission's
preliminary orders for electric certificate-of-convenience-and-necessity cases reflects Commission
precedent established for almost 20 years.13 The Commission's policy is whether the application
contains an adequate number of reasonably differentiated alternative routes to conduct a reasoned
choice of route considering all the facts and circumstances presented.14 The Commission also
recognizes that there may be circumstances that justify a limited number of alternative routes,
including the endpoint. 15 „In that event, an application must provide a reasonable explanation of
those circumstances and a reasoned justification for the limited number of routes. „16 The
applicants provided evidence showing that they presented an adequate number of reasonably
differentiated alternative routes considering all the facts and circumstances presented. Although
there is a limited number of corridors in the study area, the applicants provided a reasoned
justification for the routes as proposed.

        Therefore, because Save the Lampasas and 4K Land and Cattle Company have not shown
that they are entitled to a route adequacy hearing or that the ALJs' order was in error, the
Commission denies their appeals of Order No. 13.
